data.label: Staff browser
data.description: Staff member's browser. This is a client reference, not a provisioned service.

data.label: Web app
data.description: Browser channel (required scope). It owns private S3 assets and CloudFront access control, uses authorization code with PKCE, and shows answers with citations.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: User pool with admin-created users, required software-token MFA, an access-token scope, and catalog-backed identity and employee-region mapping. Users are onboarded with the operator tool.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Authenticated, bounded HTTP API with a JWT browser route. There is no anonymous access. Access logs support the audit trail.

data.label: Keyword RAG function
data.description: Keyword retrieval with ACL and region filtering and revision rechecks, then a cited answer that is returned through the API. It owns its execution role, logs, version and alias. Unknown identities fail closed.

data.label: Document catalog
data.description: Holds up to 100 small UTF-8 documents with explicit ACLs, revisions, tombstones for deletes and a sync checkpoint. Writes are conditional.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Existing Bedrock direct model, selected by a required model-ID input. Model access, Converse support, quotas and regional availability are not yet verified.

data.label: SharePoint (test server)
data.description: Existing SharePoint, represented here by the approved local normalized source-contract test server. It provides snapshots, ACLs, updates and deletes. The native API and real-tenant compatibility are not verified.

data.label: Confluence (test server)
data.description: Existing Confluence, represented here by the approved local normalized source-contract test server. The native API and real-tenant compatibility are not verified.

data.label: Later: Microsoft Teams channel
data.description: Teams is a deferred channel for a later phase. It is not part of this deployment.

discovery.problem: Cited answers from approved SharePoint/Confluence documents through a web app. Preserve permissions, updates and deletes. Include recovery and audit. Teams comes later.

brief.application: Design an AWS knowledge assistant that reads approved documents from existing SharePoint and Confluence systems and provides cited answers through a web application, with Teams as a later channel. Preserve source permissions, updates and deletes. For this stage use the approved local normalized source-contract test servers and bounded keyword retrieval. Keep the requested web application as required scope; an HTTP API alone does not complete that channel. Treat those existing systems as external dependencies; include recovery and audit behavior without claiming native vendor API or real tenant compatibility. Use AWS for this synthetic qualification design. Propose Sydney as a candidate region, but do not record that as an approved deployment region. Draw the architecture and identify the next missing decision. This is a test design, not an instruction to deploy.

lastAsked.question: Where do the files live, and roughly how many are there?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “SharePoint and a shared drive, about 20,000 files”.

requirements.statement: Answers may use only documents the signed-in user is allowed to open, based on explicit ACLs copied from the source snapshot. Unknown identities or missing ACLs fail closed.
requirements.rationale: Without this, the assistant could reveal restricted content. The test servers do not prove native group expansion or inherited permissions, so production stays blocked until those are verified.
requirements.basis: User: "Preserve source permissions, updates and deletes."

requirements.statement: Source updates and deletes reach the catalog through conditional writes and a recovery checkpoint, and revisions are rechecked before an answer is returned.
requirements.rationale: Stale or deleted documents could otherwise be cited. The checkpoint lets an interrupted sync resume without losing changes.
requirements.basis: User: "Preserve source permissions, updates and deletes" and "include recovery and audit behavior".

requirements.statement: Proposed: record who asked, which documents were cited and sync outcomes in logs with a retention period to be agreed.
requirements.rationale: An audit trail lets us show which sources supported an answer and investigate access questions. The retention period is still unknown.

decisions.subject: design.aws-bounded-keyword-rag-knowledge-assistant-qualification-design
decisions.title: AWS bounded keyword RAG knowledge assistant (qualification design)
decisions.context: Scope: a web app with Cognito sign-in (PKCE and MFA) calls an IAM/JWT-protected HTTP API. The API calls a bounded keyword-RAG Lambda, which reads a DynamoDB catalog and calls an existing Bedrock model to produce cited answers. SharePoint and Confluence are existing external systems, reached only through the approved local normalized source-contract test servers. This does not verify native vendor APIs, real tenants, group expansion or inherited permissions, so production stays blocked. Teams is deferred and shown as a note. Assumptions: keyword retrieval, not vector search; up to 100 small UTF-8 documents. The region is unselected (Sydney ap-southeast-2 is only a candidate), and the model ID, quotas and availability are unverified. Nothing is deployed.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
